page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded capabilities alongside moderate multi-threaded execution. The processor achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-threaded performance scales less competitively, with both Geekbench multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET benchmarks and Passmark database tests, consistently register in the average tier.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, this server is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and text processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and NVMe storage. It is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded compilation or large-scale LLM inference, where prompt processing speeds for medium-sized models drop significantly. The configuration offers a balanced resource density for standard application hosting and database operations without the overhead of specialized compute or GPU hardware.
